scenes.headline: How one GPU kernel can run a whole model
scenes.sub: Hyperkernel's release ships 42 prebuilt megakernels and a host.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Stannic! Hyperstition released forty-two megakernels for the B300. Here's how one kernel runs a whole model.

scenes.text: Launch one kernel with a block per processor, never let it exit, and hand it work through a ring in memory.
scenes.say: Launch one kernel with a block for every processor, never let it exit, and hand it work through a ring.

scenes.title: From a checkpoint to a resident kernel

steps.say: The host knows nothing about the model. It copies each tensor to the address the plan names.
Then it launches one function, a hundred and forty-eight blocks, with every layer unrolled inside.
For the language model server, that kernel never returns. Requests arrive through a ring.
Each kernel is straight-line code for one exact shape: one per concurrency, one per protein length.

scenes.title: Three ways the host launches
scenes.say: The host launches in three patterns.

items.say: Once, fed through a ring, for DeepSeek and pi zero FAST.
Once per call, for the robot policy, openpilot and a training step.
Or several per call. A protein fold is nine launches.

scenes.title: The one number the repo contains
scenes.text: MFU = flops x tokens / (time x 8 x peak)

parts.say: Flops per token: six times the active parameters, plus causal attention.
The step time is the repo's own report.
The peak is eight GPUs at two point two five petaflops.

scenes.label: Qwen3-30B training MFU, recomputed from the bundle
scenes.note: Conservative count: causal attention, no embedding
scenes.say: The bundle's parameter count reproduces thirty point six percent exactly, with conservative counting.

scenes.label: Models named in the thread with a shipped kernel

scenes.say: The kernels are real and their correctness logs are careful. The speedups need their baselines released.
